facts.statement: Borealonectes is a genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid, which is a type of plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Borealonectes is a genus of rhomaleosaurid pliosauroid, a type of plesiosaur.

facts.statement: Borealonectes lived during the Callovian age of the Middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago.
facts.quote: Its fossils were found in the Callovian-age (Middle Jurassic, about 165-161 million years ago) Hiccles Cove Formation of Melville Island, Canada

facts.statement: The description of Borealonectes is based on the skull, neck vertebrae, and right forelimb of a single individual.
facts.quote: It is based on a skull, neck vertebrae, and the right forelimb of one individual.

facts.statement: The genus Borealonectes was named in 2008 by Sato and Wu.
facts.quote: Named in 2008 by Sato and Wu

facts.statement: Borealonectes is one of the few plesiosaur species known from the Jurassic period of North America.
facts.quote: Borealonectes is one of the few plesiosaurs known from the Jurassic of North America

facts.statement: Borealonectes is the first marine reptile from the Canadian Arctic known to have a well-preserved skull.
facts.quote: and the first marine reptile from the Canadian Arctic with a well-preserved skull.

facts.statement: Borealonectes belongs to the family Rhomaleosauridae.
The time range for Borealonectes is the Callovian stage, from 165.3 to 161.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Callovian (165.3 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: The name Borealonectes means "northern swimmer" in Greek.
Fossils of Borealonectes were found in the Hiccles Cove Formation on Melville Island, Canada, dating to the Middle Jurassic Callovian age, about 165 to 161 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles encontrados datan de la edad del Calloviense (Jurásico medio, hace unos 165-161 millones de años), en la formación Hiccles Cove de la isla Melville, Canadá
